item.content:encoded:
A Homeland Security Investigations agent has been arrested and is facing multiple child sex abuse charges following an investigation in Spanish Fort, Alabama. According to WKRG News 5, Kent Blacklidge turned himself in to the Baldwin County Jail on Saturday.

Spanish Fort Police Chief John Barber and Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall addressed the arrest and pending prosecution during a public statement. Details about the specific charges and investigation remain limited, but authorities have indicated the case involves serious allegations against the federal agent.

The arrest represents a significant development in what appears to be an ongoing investigation into criminal conduct by a federal law enforcement officer. The case is now moving through the prosecution phase, with further details expected to emerge as court proceedings advance.

item.title: Fill the Mayflower in Pensacola to Support Local Families
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: Some neighbors in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will head into winter unsure where the next healthy meal will come from. On Friday, November 20, 2026, the Pensacola community has a simple way to help change that. NewsRadio Pensacola is proud to join Manna Food Pantries and Coastal Moving & Storage for Fill the Mayflower in Pensacola to Support…
item.content:encoded:
Some neighbors in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will head into winter unsure where the next healthy meal will come from. On Friday, November 20, 2026, the Pensacola community has a simple way to help change that.


NewsRadio Pensacola is proud to join Manna Food Pantries and Coastal Moving & Storage for Fill the Mayflower in Pensacola to Support Local Families, an annual food and funds drive that helps provide nutritious food to children, families, senior citizens, veterans and individuals facing hunger across Northwest Florida.


The event will take place at Cordova Mall in Pensacola, where supporters can drive up, donate food or funds, and help fill the Mayflower truck for local neighbors in need.



A local food drive with a clear purpose


Fill the Mayflower is one of Manna Food Pantries’ largest food drives of the year. The food collected helps Manna serve people experiencing hunger through the winter months, a time when household budgets can become especially tight.


For many families, the need is basic and immediate. Groceries, rent, utilities, transportation and medical costs can all compete for the same paycheck. A few extra bags of healthy food can give a parent breathing room. A monetary gift can help provide meals for a senior citizen. A box of shelf-stable items can help a veteran, a child or an individual facing a hard season.

Manna helped 71,005 people during 2025, and the need for nutritious food continues across Northwest Florida.


A $25 donation can provide five days of food for a child in need. A $50 donation can provide 30 healthy meals for a senior citizen.

That kind of impact is why Fill the Mayflower matters. The event turns individual donations into a community-wide response to hunger.


When and where to donate


Fill the Mayflower will be held on Friday, November 20, 2026, at Cordova Mall in Pensacola.


Detail

Information

Date

Friday, November 20, 2026

Location

Dillard’s parking lot at Cordova Mall

Address

5100 North Ninth Avenue, Pensacola, Florida

Specific area

South of BJ’s Restaurant

Donation method

Drive up and remain in your vehicle while volunteers unload donations


The setup is designed to make donating quick and convenient. Supporters may remain inside their vehicles while volunteers unload food donations at the Mayflower truck. That means people can stop by during their day, drop off what they can, and be on their way.


The Cordova Mall location also makes the event easy to include in a regular errand run. A few extra nonperishable items added to a grocery trip can become part of a much larger effort to care for local families.


What Manna can accept


Manna appreciates all unopened, commercially packaged, nonperishable food donations. The focus is on healthy items that can be stored safely and distributed to people who need them.


Good donation choices may include shelf-stable foods such as:


  • Canned vegetables and fruit

  • Canned beans

  • Canned tuna, chicken or other proteins

  • Peanut butter

  • Shelf-stable milk

  • Oatmeal

  • Whole-grain cereal

  • Rice

  • Pasta

  • Canned soups

  • Macaroni and cheese

  • Healthy snack items

  • Baby food in unopened commercial packaging


When choosing items, think about foods that are filling, easy to prepare and useful for many kinds of households. Pull-tab cans can be helpful for people who may not have a can opener. Lower-sodium options, whole-grain items and protein-rich foods can also support more balanced meals.


A practical way to build a donation bag is to imagine a few simple meals. Pasta with canned vegetables and protein. Oatmeal and fruit. Beans and rice. Peanut butter with whole-grain crackers. Small combinations like these can help Manna provide more complete support.


What Manna cannot accept


For safety and quality reasons, Manna cannot accept every item. Before donating, check that food is unopened, clearly labeled and commercially packaged.


Manna cannot accept:


  • Alcoholic beverages

  • Homemade food

  • Noncommercial canned or packaged goods

  • Perishable items

  • Previously opened or used items

  • Rusty cans

  • Unlabeled cans


These guidelines help protect the people who receive food and make it easier for volunteers and staff to sort donations. If an item has been opened, repackaged at home, left unmarked or stored in a damaged container, it should not be donated.


This is especially important during large food drives. Clear, safe donations allow the team to move food quickly from collection to sorting to distribution.



Monetary gifts help too


Food donations are a major part of Fill the Mayflower, but monetary donations are also welcome. Cash, checks and credit or debit cards will be accepted at the event.


Financial gifts give Manna flexibility. Food pantries often need to fill specific gaps, respond to changing demand and source nutritious foods that may not arrive through donation bins. A monetary gift can help provide exactly what is needed at the right time.


Even a modest donation can make a real difference. According to Manna, $25 can provide five days of food for a child in need, and $50 can provide 30 healthy meals for a senior citizen.


That makes Fill the Mayflower accessible to many kinds of donors. Some people may bring a trunk full of groceries. Others may give a few dollars. Both forms of support matter, because both help Manna serve local neighbors.


Why healthy nonperishable food matters


When people think of food drives, they often picture canned goods. Those staples are important, but nutrition matters too.


Healthy nonperishable food helps families do more than get through the day. It can support children who need steady meals to focus at school. It can help older adults stretch fixed incomes while still eating regularly. It can help working families make it to the next paycheck with less stress.


Shelf-stable food also plays a special role during the winter months. Holiday expenses, colder weather and higher household costs can create extra pressure. Food collected through Fill the Mayflower helps Manna continue serving people during a season when many families need additional support.


A strong donation does not have to be complicated. Think durable, unopened and useful. Foods with protein, fiber and familiar ingredients are often among the most practical choices.


A community effort across Northwest Florida


Fill the Mayflower brings together local organizations, media partners, volunteers and donors for a shared purpose. NewsRadio Pensacola is joining Manna Food Pantries and Coastal Moving & Storage to help encourage support for the annual drive.


The event is made possible by Coastal Moving & Storage and media partners Cat Country 98.7, NewsRadio 92.3 and WEAR 3.


That broad support reflects the scale of the need. Hunger does not affect only one kind of household. It can touch children, parents, seniors, veterans and individuals in many different circumstances. Some people need short-term help after a job loss, medical bill or emergency. Others face longer periods of food insecurity.


Food drives like this give the wider community a direct way to respond. A donation made in a parking lot in Pensacola can become part of a pantry visit for a neighbor in Escambia or Santa Rosa County.


How to make your donation count


A little planning can make a donation more useful and easier to sort.


Before heading to Cordova Mall, take a few minutes to check each item. Make sure packages are sealed. Look for clear labels and expiration dates. Avoid dented, rusty or unlabeled cans. Keep glass containers to a minimum when possible, since they can break during transport.


It can also help to pack similar items together. Cans in one box, dry goods in another, and lighter items such as cereal or pasta on top. If donating by car, place bags or boxes in the trunk or back seat where volunteers can reach them easily.


For families with children, this can also be a meaningful learning moment. Kids can help choose healthy foods, count items or pack bags. The experience can show that helping others can be simple, practical and local.


Groups can take part too. Friends, civic clubs, faith communities and workplaces can collect items ahead of the event and deliver them together. A group effort can quickly turn a few pantry staples into a large donation.


What to expect when you arrive


The event is designed for convenience. Donors should go to the Dillard’s parking lot at Cordova Mall, south of BJ’s Restaurant. From there, volunteers will help unload donations at the Mayflower truck.


Supporters may remain inside their vehicles while donations are collected. That helps keep traffic moving and makes the process easier for people with children, mobility needs or packed schedules.


If donating funds, cash, checks and credit or debit cards will be accepted at the event. If donating food, make sure items meet Manna’s donation guidelines before arrival.


Because no event hours were included in the announcement, supporters should check Manna’s event information for the latest details before going.



Help fill the truck on November 20


Fill the Mayflower is a simple invitation with a meaningful result. Bring healthy, nonperishable food. Make a monetary gift if that is the best way to help. Encourage a neighbor, friend or group to do the same.


On Friday, November 20, 2026, NewsRadio Pensacola will join Manna Food Pantries and Coastal Moving & Storage at Cordova Mall to help fill the Mayflower truck for Northwest Florida neighbors facing hunger.


For event details and updates, visit Manna Food Pantries’ page for Fill the Mayflower.


A single bag of groceries may not feel large on its own. Combined with hundreds of other gifts from across the community, it can help carry local families through the winter months with dignity, care and nutritious food.

item.title: Santa Rosa County proposes $256M budget with tax adjustments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County officials are moving forward with budget discussions as the Office of Management and Budget prepares to present its proposed 2027 spending plan to the Board of County Commissioners, according to WKRG News 5. The $256 million budget proposal includes changes to the county's tax structure, though specifics on those adjustments were…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County officials are moving forward with budget discussions as the Office of Management and Budget prepares to present its proposed 2027 spending plan to the Board of County Commissioners, according to WKRG News 5.

The $256 million budget proposal includes changes to the county's tax structure, though specifics on those adjustments were not immediately detailed. The presentation will happen during a public hearing, giving residents and commissioners a chance to weigh in on the county's financial priorities for the coming year.

Budget season typically involves discussions about everything from road maintenance and public safety to schools and emergency services. Santa Rosa County commissioners will have the opportunity to ask questions and hear from the public before moving toward final approval.

This comes as counties across Northwest Florida continue navigating post-pandemic spending patterns and inflation's impact on operating costs. Exact dates and details on the specific tax changes should be available through Santa Rosa County's official channels.

item.title: Arrests Made in Destin Home Invasion; Woman Still Missing

Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to the scene and apprehended two individuals connected to the robbery. However, investigators…
item.content:encoded:
Two suspects are now in custody following a home invasion in Destin on Friday morning, but law enforcement continues to search for a woman who was present during the incident, according to WKRG News 5.

Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to the scene and apprehended two individuals connected to the robbery. However, investigators say a female resident was in the apartment at the time of the invasion and remains unaccounted for.

The Sheriff's Office has not released details about the suspects' identities, specific charges, or the circumstances surrounding the woman's disappearance. Authorities are urging anyone with information about the missing woman or the home invasion to contact the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office.

Troopers say he was crossing the road near a Casey's gas station when a southbound sedan driven by a seventy-seven-year-old woman hit him. He was taken to the hospital, where he later died. item.content:encoded: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Longtime Emerald Coast Utilities Authority board member Dale Perkins has died at sixty-four. Perkins served on the ECUA board for thirty-two years, first taking office in 1994, and had chosen not to seek reelection this year. A commemorative plaque honoring his tenure was dedicated near Pensacola Beach earlier this year. Outside his public service, Perkins worked as a social worker, substance abuse counselor, and local fishing boat captain. He's survived by his daughters, mother, and seven siblings.

item.title: ECUA Board Member Dale Perkins Dies at 64
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Walter "Dale" Perkins, who spent three decades shaping water policy across North Escambia, died Sunday at age 64. Perkins served on the Emerald Coast Utilities Authority Board representing District 4 for 32 years, beginning his tenure in 1994. He had announced he would not seek reelection, with his final term set to expire in November. During his…
item.content:encoded:
Walter "Dale" Perkins, who spent three decades shaping water policy across North Escambia, died Sunday at age 64. Perkins served on the Emerald Coast Utilities Authority Board representing District 4 for 32 years, beginning his tenure in 1994. He had announced he would not seek reelection, with his final term set to expire in November.

During his time on the ECUA Board, Perkins was involved in decisions affecting water service and infrastructure across the northern part of the county. His lengthy tenure reflected deep roots in the community and a sustained commitment to utility management during a period of significant growth in the region.

The ECUA will need to fill the District 4 seat following Perkins' passing and the expiration of his term this fall.

Tuesday night will see partly cloudy skies with a low around 73 degrees as winds diminish to calm before turning light and easterly after…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola area residents can expect pleasant conditions through Tuesday, with mostly sunny skies and a high near 90 degrees. Light east winds between 5 and 10 mph will keep things comfortable throughout the day.

Tuesday night will see partly cloudy skies with a low around 73 degrees as winds diminish to calm before turning light and easterly after midnight.

The pattern shifts Wednesday, however. Showers are likely to develop after 1 p.m., with the possibility of thunderstorms moving through the area. Highs will be slightly cooler at 89 degrees. If you're planning outdoor activities, Tuesday appears to be the better bet, with Wednesday better suited for indoor plans or staying prepared for wet weather.

item.title: Escambia County Considers 12-Month Data Center Moratorium
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Commission is moving toward scheduling a public hearing on a proposed 12-month moratorium on data center development, according to North Escambia reporting. The potential moratorium would mark the county's latest action in an ongoing effort to restrict data center growth in the area. Commissioners are expected to take up the…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Commission is moving toward scheduling a public hearing on a proposed 12-month moratorium on data center development, according to North Escambia reporting.

The potential moratorium would mark the county's latest action in an ongoing effort to restrict data center growth in the area. Commissioners are expected to take up the measure this week, with a public hearing likely to follow if the initial motion passes.

Data centers have become an increasingly contentious issue in Escambia County, with county leadership expressing concerns about the facilities' impact on infrastructure, utilities, and community character. A moratorium would halt new approvals while county staff and commissioners evaluate long-term zoning and development policies.

The hearing would give residents and stakeholders a chance to weigh in on the proposal before commissioners make a final decision on the moratorium's terms and duration.

item.title: Cancer Survivor, 5, Cheers with Tate High Aggies
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Kinslee is a four-year cancer survivor who was diagnosed with Wilms tumor, a rare form of kidney cancer that typically affects young children. The North Escambia student's appearance…
item.content:encoded:
Five-year-old Kinslee Gibson got the chance to live out a special moment Friday night when she joined the Tate High School cheerleaders on the sidelines for a game. Kinslee is a four-year cancer survivor who was diagnosed with Wilms tumor, a rare form of kidney cancer that typically affects young children.

The North Escambia student's appearance with the Aggie cheerleaders marked a celebration of her ongoing recovery and resilience. Wilms tumor diagnoses can be frightening for families, but advances in treatment have improved survival rates significantly over the past two decades.

Friday's game gave Kinslee a chance to be part of the Tate High community and experience the energy of a high school football or athletic event alongside the school's cheerleading squad. For a five-year-old cancer survivor, moments like these represent milestones worth celebrating.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Beach saw plenty of visitors and locals taking advantage of ideal holiday weather on Labor Day, with clear skies and warm temperatures bringing out beachgoers across the sand and water.

According to WKRG News 5, the pleasant conditions — combined with green flag warnings indicating safe swimming — made for a popular day at the beach. The combination of sunshine and heat drew residents and visitors looking to make the most of the long weekend.

The strong turnout underscores Pensacola Beach's appeal as a destination during peak summer and early fall season, when weather patterns often favor clear conditions and calm waters.

item.content:encoded:
Labor Day marks the unofficial kickoff to a four-month stretch filled with holidays, celebrations, and community events that'll keep Pensacola residents busy through the New Year. According to WKRG News 5, while the season offers plenty of opportunities for fun and connection, it also comes with its share of responsibilities that deserve attention.

The months ahead bring everything from local festivals and family gatherings to year-end festivities. News 5's Drexel Gilbert noted that balancing the excitement of the season with the practical demands it creates is key to making the most of the time.

Whether you're planning holiday travel, attending community events, or managing family obligations, experts recommend getting ahead on planning. That means mapping out your calendar early, budgeting for seasonal expenses, and thinking through logistics before the rush hits. The holiday season can sneak up fast once Labor Day passes.

item.title: Multi-vehicle ATV crash in Okaloosa County requires air rescue response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Emergency crews responded to a serious multi-vehicle crash involving an all-terrain vehicle in Okaloosa County on Saturday, according to the Holt Fire District. Multiple emergency units were dispatched to the scene, with fire rescue crews providing initial response. The crash was significant enough to warrant a call for medevac assistance,…
item.content:encoded:
Emergency crews responded to a serious multi-vehicle crash involving an all-terrain vehicle in Okaloosa County on Saturday, according to the Holt Fire District.

Multiple emergency units were dispatched to the scene, with fire rescue crews providing initial response. The crash was significant enough to warrant a call for medevac assistance, indicating at least one person required transport by medical helicopter.

The Holt Fire District confirmed the incident on social media but did not immediately release details about the number of people injured or the exact circumstances of the crash. The incident underscores the ongoing safety concerns around ATV operation in the region, particularly when multiple vehicles are involved.
